recognize_zh: 高倍可見多顆帶狀或分葉少的嗜中性球，部分細胞質有粗大毒性顆粒，另有兩個星芒狀、中央紫色顆粒、周邊淡藍並有小空泡的大團塊，疑為大型血小板或血小板聚集，符合 G-CSF 反應。
features: Several band and hyposegmented neutrophils; lower-left cells show coarse dark toxic granulation
Upper neutrophils have paler, less granular cytoplasm
Two large irregular stellate bodies with central purple granular material, pale blue periphery and small vacuoles, favored giant platelets or platelet aggregates
No nucleus identified within the stellate bodies
Red cells normocytic and normochromic without significant poikilocytosis
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows increased neutrophils, predominantly band and hyposegmented forms, several with coarse toxic granulation. Two large, irregular, stellate anucleate bodies with central purple granules and a pale vacuolated periphery are present, favored to represent giant platelets or small platelet clumps. Red cells are unremarkable. In a patient receiving growth factor, findings are consistent with G-CSF effect with toxic granulation and left shift.

ddx.vs: Neutrophil changes are identical, so clinical history of G-CSF versus infection distinguishes them.
Micromegakaryocytes contain a dense hypolobated nucleus, which is not seen in these anucleate stellate bodies.
Dysplastic hypolobated neutrophils are typically hypogranular with clumped chromatin, rather than showing coarse toxic granules.
